A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same InternSVG–SAgoge–SArena work. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching material moved or renumbered in v3.

before.justification: v1 reports original InternSVG evaluations on SArena and SGP-Bench, multitask and training-strategy ablations, and qualitative results in Section 5 and Appendix B.

after.justification: v3 retains those experiments and adds external benchmark evaluations, component ablations, cross-domain transfer, code-quality analysis, and a human study.

M1.justification: The architecture, SVG-specific vocabulary, subword-averaged embedding initialization, and two-stage training procedure remain unchanged in Section 4 and Appendix A. New ablation variants test existing components; expanded annotation descriptions do not establish a changed method.

E1.justification: v3 adds evaluation on SVG-Stack for image-to-SVG and UniSVG for understanding and generation, previously only discussed as related resources. Appendix B.10 also introduces human assessment involving researchers, PhD students, and UI designers. The original SAgoge and SArena domains and dataset sizes are retained.

E2.justification: Six InternVL3.5 sizes are added to SArena-Icon generation comparisons in v3 Table 12, although several already appeared in v1's illustration or editing tables. The new external comparisons also include GPT-4V, StarVector 1B, LLaMA-3.2-3B, and fine-tuned LLaMA/Qwen baselines, substantially extending the evaluated comparator configurations.

E3.justification: New protocols include component ablations using 50% of selected stage-two data, icon-only training followed by chemistry evaluation, and structural-count and inference-time measurements. v3 also adds success-rate metrics and a 42-participant study with blinded caption comparisons, randomized output ordering, and 1–5 ratings. These additions substantially extend evaluation design; the original training settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Section 5.4 extends the existing token-length and training-loss illustrations with task-level Raw/T/T+E component ablations. Appendices B.6, B.8, and B.10 add analyses of code structure and efficiency, zero-shot icon-to-chemistry transfer, synthetic-data quality, and human judgments of generated outputs.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance-testing procedures. The new human-study ratings and success percentages are point estimates; participant counts and sampling procedures change evaluation design rather than uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: v3 adds extensive benchmark, ablation, transfer, code-quality, success-rate, and human-evaluation results, including a UniSVG Final Score of 0.826. Reported FVDs also change: Table 4's InternSVG value becomes 99.474 instead of 207.935, matching v1's appendix, while the one-stage ablation changes from 237.524 to 101.433. These reporting changes do not establish improvements from retraining the same model.

T1.justification: The embedding-initialization equation and associated mathematical content are unchanged. Neither version introduces theoretical propositions or proofs; v3's new metrics and analyses are empirical.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list, and conclusion retain the same dataset–benchmark–model contribution, dataset-scale claims, unified-modeling benefits, and broad performance claims. The new experiments principally support these existing claims.

C2.justification: v3 adds substantive interpretations connecting primitive diversity and concise SVG structure to editability and inference efficiency (B.6), external and zero-shot results to broader generalization (B.5/B.8), and human judgments to synthetic-data reliability and practical usability (B.10). These extend v1's interpretation beyond visual fidelity and cross-task transfer.

D1.justification: Section 3.1.2 newly specifies training/test annotator assignments, template-based editing verification, a 147-color palette, and CLIP similarity above 0.8 for style-transfer pairing. v3 also provides human-study instruments and discloses assistive LLM use. These improve documentation without demonstrating changed data construction; existing training hyperparameters, hardware, prompt templates, and project link remain.

R1.justification: v3 adds the InternVL3.5 reference and relates its new code-quality analysis to SVGenius's complexity metrics and StarVector's primitive representations. The main related-work discussion and novelty positioning remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 expands the annotation explanation and experimental discussion, adds appendix subsections and reproducibility, ethics, and LLM-use statements, and standardizes some model names. Most existing prose and the main narrative structure are retained; this is a localized expansion rather than an extensive rewrite.

P2.justification: v3 adds substantial visual reporting through component-ablation, external-benchmark, transfer, code-quality, and human-evaluation tables, questionnaire screenshots, and eight rating plots. Existing generation tables gain success-rate columns and baseline rows. Qualitative panels are redistributed or resized, while their underlying examples are retained.

improvement.justification: v3 substantially strengthens validation of the unchanged proposal. Table 7 directly tests the tokenization and initialization components; external generation benchmarks and cross-domain transfer address generalization beyond SArena; and Appendix B.10 supplies human evidence for synthetic-data reliability and practical output quality. These address important evidential gaps in v1, while numerical reconciliations improve consistency. Statistical uncertainty remains unreported and some numerical prose inconsistencies persist, but the additions materially improve the paper's empirical support.
